name: Victoria
description: Seychelles' capital on the northeast coast, small enough to cross on foot in twenty minutes, with the clocktower that is a miniature of one on London's Vauxhall Bridge Road, the Sir Selwyn Selwyn-Clarke market and the government offices.
bestFor: Anyone needing banks, the market and the bus network
pros: The market is where local prices actually are
cons: Very quiet after dark and at weekends
No beach in the town itself
Little accommodation aimed at long stays

name: Beau Vallon
tagline: The main beach, on the northwest coast
description: The long crescent of sand on the northwestern shore, with the island's concentration of hotels, restaurants and dive operators, and the calmest swimming during the southeast trade wind season. It is where most visitors to Mahe stay.
bestFor: Anyone who wants the main beach and the dive operators
pros: The most swimmable beach on Mahe
Restaurants, dive shops and a Wednesday market
cons: The most expensive part of the island

name: The South of Mahe
tagline: Anse Royale, Baie Lazare and the quiet end
description: The southern half of the island, with Anse Royale on the east coast, Baie Lazare and Anse Soleil on the west, and a string of small beaches between granite headlands. It is considerably cheaper and quieter than the northwest.
bestFor: Longer stays wanting the best value on the island
pros: The most beautiful small beaches on Mahe
cons: Forty minutes from Victoria by bus

name: Morne Seychellois
tagline: The mountain interior, in cloud forest
description: The national park covering a fifth of Mahe, rising to over nine hundred metres through cloud forest with trails up to Morne Blanc and the Copolia viewpoint. A handful of guesthouses sit on the slopes with views down to both coasts.
bestFor: Walkers who want cooler air and forest rather than a beach

name: Praslin and La Digue
tagline: The other islands, an hour by ferry
description: The two neighbouring islands, reached from Mahe by ferry in about an hour. Praslin holds the Vallee de Mai with its coco de mer palms, and La Digue has Anse Source d'Argent, the granite-boulder beach that appears on every list of the world's best.
bestFor: Anyone whose reason for coming is the beaches everyone has seen
pros: Anse Source d'Argent and Anse Lazio
The Vallee de Mai and the coco de mer
Bicycles rather than cars on La Digue
cons: More expensive than the south of Mahe
